en: Drinking water prevents heatstroke during sunny recess because sweating cools your body through evaporation.
Earthquakes happen when tectonic plates suddenly slip, so dropping and covering under a sturdy desk protects you from falling debris.
Loam soil is best for planting vegetables because it holds enough water and nutrients for healthy plant roots.
Stagnant rainwater breeds mosquitoes that carry dengue, so emptying containers around your house prevents this dangerous disease.
Minerals like zinc oxide in sunscreen reflect harmful ultraviolet rays from the sun to protect your skin.
The Sun emits ultraviolet radiation, so wearing a wide-brimmed hat prevents painful sunburns during outdoor recess.
Typhoons bring heavy rain causing flash floods, so moving to higher ground keeps your family safe.
The Moon's gravity creates high tides that can trap people on sandbars, so always check tide schedules before exploring beaches.
The tropical climate has high humidity, meaning you must drink extra water to avoid dehydration during outdoor activities.
Lightning travels through conductive materials like metal, so staying away from fences and umbrellas during a thunderstorm prevents electric shocks.
The North Star, Polaris, stays fixed in the northern sky, helping lost hikers find their direction at night.
Planting trees on steep slopes prevents landslides because their deep roots hold the heavy, wet soil firmly together.
